sources: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 231883 (search/campsites API, read 2026-10-28)
Esri World_Imagery around the catalog site points

values.note: $15 a site (2026 and 2027 peak seasons). A $10 car pass, collected at the Maroon Bells Welcome Station as you enter, is required on top of the camping fee. 8 people and two cars per site.

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/silver-queen-campground ('Single Site: $15 per night'; '8 person, two car limit per campsite'; vehicle pass sentence) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/231883 (notice '$10 car pass is required in addition to camping fee and will be collected as you enter the area.') + /rates (Peak Season 2026-05-22 to 2026-09-30: STANDARD NONELECTRIC 15; 2027 the same), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Five sites. FS: '30-foot RV limit'. Catalog: 001, 002 and 004 RV/trailer 30 ft, 005 25 ft, 003 tent only (25 ft pull-through spur).

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/silver-queen-campground ('Silver Queen Campground has five campsites available for advanced reservation which are able to accommodate tents, trailers, and RVs (30-foot RV limit).') + recreation.gov catalog for 231883 (permitted equipment lengths per site), read 2026-10-28

hookups.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/silver-queen-campground ('Electrical hook-ups are not available.') + recreation.gov catalog (no hookup attributes on any site), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Bear-proof food lockers at each site and bear-proof trash receptacles. Drinking water: the FS and recreation.gov descriptions list it, but the FS amenity table says 'Potable water is not available at this site.'

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/silver-queen-campground ('Sites are equipped with picnic tables, vault toilets, campfire rings and drinking water'; 'Vault Toilets'; 'Potable water is not available at this site.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/231883 ('food storage lockers (bear boxes), campfire rings and drinking water'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: All five sites reservable on recreation.gov at least 4 days ahead. 'Five day' stay limit (recreation.gov: 4 nights in a rolling 30 days). Reservations must check in at the Maroon Bells Welcome Station (7 a.m.-7 p.m.) within 24 hours or the site is forfeited. 2026 reservation season May 22 - Sept 30 (2027: May 28 - Sept 30). Check-out 11 a.m. (recreation.gov) or 2 p.m. (FS).

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/silver-queen-campground ('five campsites available for advanced reservation'; '5 day stay limit . Check out time is 2:00 p.m.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/231883 (rules maxStay 4 nights 'Rolling 30 Days', reservationCutOff 4; notices 'Check out time is 11:00 a.m.', check-in within 24 hours) + /rates (Peak Season 2026-05-22 to 2026-09-30), read 2026-10-28

note: White River NF (Aspen-Sopris RD) campground in the Maroon Bells Scenic Area, 6.5 mi southwest of Aspen on Maroon Creek Rd, in aspen a short walk from Maroon Creek, with views of Pyramid Peak. Campers drive in on a vehicle pass bought at the Maroon Bells Welcome Station. --Claude
summary: FS page + recreation.gov + catalog: confirmed 5 sites, 30-ft RV limit (now agency-stated), $15, reservable. Added no hookups, vault toilets, $10 car pass, booking (4-day cutoff, 4-night limit, reservation season May 22-Sept 30), fees checked 2026. Potable water left unset (FS page contradicts itself). Note rewritten: field facts dropped, 'along the Maroon Creek' corrected to the agencies' 'a short walk from Maroon Creek'.
flags: Phone missing: Aspen-Sopris Ranger District (970) 963-2266 (FS page office contact, Carbondale; also recreation.gov's facility phone). recreation.gov's contact info gives (970) 945-2521 (the Supervisor's Office per the Maroon Bells Scenic Area page).
Website: stored only the recreation.gov listing; the campground's FS page is https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/whiteriver/recreation/silver-queen-campground.

Water conflict: FS description 'Sites are equipped with picnic tables, vault toilets, campfire rings and drinking water' (recreation.gov the same), but the FS amenity table says 'Potable water is not available at this site.' potable_water left unset.

Maroon Creek Rd access (visitmaroonbells.com, 2026): 'The Maroon Bells Scenic Area is closed to inbound private vehicles from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM between May 22nd and October 18th'; 'Those with campground reservations do not need a reservation to park at the Maroon Lake Trailhead.'; 'Starting November 10th, the Maroon Creek Road will be closed for the winter season ... typically on May 15th.' FS: campers 'must purchase a vehicle pass to drive to their designated campground at the Welcome Station across from the Silver Bar Campground.' Neither says whether campers are exempt from the 8-5 inbound closure.

Waterfront (stored not waterfront, kept): FS and recreation.gov say 'a short walk from Maroon Creek'. On Esri imagery a creek channel passes ~20 m below site 005 and ~30-35 m east of sites 001-003, all through dense spruce/aspen canopy, so creekside cannot be earned. The old note's 'along the Maroon Creek' overstated it.
Elevation: recreation.gov says 8,460 ft, the FS page 8,700 ft (stored 2,660 m = 8,727 ft). Pin 39.1294,-106.9018 is ~10 m from the catalog site centroid. Fine.
Season: no statement of when the campground itself is open; the reservation season is in booking.season.
